(Search snippet content — full article 403'd on direct fetch; Bloomberg's own reporting language)
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood granted migrant care workers a reprieve from plans for tighter immigration rules, but stopped short of reversing controversial proposals to make wider reforms apply retroactively.
Her original proposals, unveiled in November 2025, would double the qualifying period for settlement for most migrants from five to 10 years, and potentially triple it to 15 for care workers.
The plan for so-called "earned settlement," which would see the base timeline migrants have to stay in the country before they can claim settled status extended to 10 years from five, will proceed and will apply to those already waiting.
Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp wrote on X: "Shabana Mahmood has been forced to surrender to Angela Rayner and the open-borders Labour left." He said she would "now allow hundreds of thousands of low-wage and no-wage migrants to stay in the UK forever and claim benefits."
Tensions in the Cabinet over the policy surfaced when Housing Secretary Angela Rayner earlier this year publicly attacked the prospect of backdating the plans.
